news.title: Free Mode and the Future of Freemium
news.gist: Free AI usage costs real money on every request, so freemium is turning from a way to win new users into a perk for paying ones: free usage layered on top of a paid plan’s credits.
points: Replit dropped its free Starter plan and gave paying users a Free Mode that sits on top of the credits they already buy
Lovable gives Pro and Business users daily free credits with no monthly cap, plus separate Cloud and AI grants
Four ways to make usage free are named: by model, by speed, by type of action and by periodic refill
LLMs now do many of the first-draft jobs that free tiers used to win users with, so free plans acquire less

news.title: Developer Tool Pricing Changes: September 14–20, 2026
news.gist: Developer free tiers shrank this week: CockroachDB stopped offering its free Basic plan to new deployments, Postman took cloud performance testing off Free, and Google kept older Gemini models for existing users only.
points: PostHog startup credits no longer pay for its AI products, such as PostHog AI and Replay Vision
Groq swapped Qwen3.6 27B for Qwen3.8 27B on free and developer plans and shut the old model ID, so code calling it breaks
Canva’s free tier moved the other way, adding a Brand Kit, Affinity access and a small allowance of AI uses
Google stopped renewing standalone Developer Program Premium subscriptions

news.why: Free tiers and startup credits can disappear for new accounts at short notice, so check current terms before building a new project on them.

news.title: 14 Trends in AI Monetization
news.gist: AI lets customers get more done with fewer seats, so vendors are moving to hybrid fees, credits and outcome pricing, while buyers accept variable bills only when the spend can be forecast.
points: Buyers prefer structured commitments such as Salesforce Pre-Commit, Workday Flex Credits and SAP AI Units to open-ended metering
Credit wallets, with balances, alerts and top-ups, are becoming a feature of the product itself
Outcome pricing such as Helply’s per-outcome rate is real, but the author doubts it goes mainstream soon
Most vendors fold MCP access into existing plans, and standalone MCP add-ons are still rare
nums: vendors that combine a fixed fee with a usage charge, up from 45% in 2023

news.why: Vendors say unpredictable bills are what stalls AI adoption, so buyers have leverage to ask for committed, forecastable AI spend instead of open metering.

news.title: Developer Tool Pricing Report: September 2026
news.gist: AgentDeals called September a hard month for developer free tiers: changes that hurt buyers far outnumbered those that helped, as limits shrank and products were retired.
points: Product deprecations were the most common change type, ahead of reduced limits
OneSignal limited free mobile push to smaller organizations, new customers first and existing ones a month later
Modal’s Starter compute allowance no longer covers Shared Endpoints
Railway, Cloudflare Workers and Browserless were the month’s few improvements

news.why: With model retirements and free-tier cuts arriving monthly, budget for migrations and paid tiers rather than assuming current free allowances will last.

patterns.t: Model costs reached list prices, in both directions
patterns.p: AI inference and generation prices followed the underlying models: hosts raised rates where demand is strong and cut credit costs where newer models are cheaper. Usage-priced AI bills can change between invoices with no plan change.

points.text: raised Qwen3.7-Max serverless inference by 25%, to $2.50 input and $7.50 output per million tokens
lifted its estimated production voice-agent rate from $0.056 to $0.06 a minute as one model’s rate rose

cut Seedance 2.0 video credit costs about in half, from 107 to 51 credits a second at 720p
replaced GPT Image 2 with two 2.5 variants, taking the lowest price per request from $0.225 to $0.035
halved its LLM Gateway base fee from $400 to $200 a month plus usage

patterns.t: Entry plans got narrower or pricier
patterns.p: Several AI and developer products cut what free or cheap plans include, or removed them, pushing small buyers to a paid or sales-led step sooner; Anthropic moved the other way. The Cockroach Labs and Pika changes come from PricingSaaS reports.

patterns.t: Fewer ways to buy, steered toward bigger bundles
patterns.p: Market leaders cut the number of ways to buy rather than list prices, and smaller vendors removed middle or top plans. Menus get simpler but cheap ways in disappear. Salesforce, Microsoft 365, Temporal and Playbook come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: Leaders repackaged; none changed a list price
stats_analysis.figNote: changes at market leaders (tier 1) that were packaging moves
stats_analysis.p: HubSpot, Anthropic, Salesforce and Microsoft 365 all changed what plans include or how they are bought, not what they cost. Two of the four (Salesforce and Microsoft 365) come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: Every list-price increase came from a smaller company
stats_analysis.figNote: changes tagged Price increase that were at smaller (tier 3) companies
stats_analysis.p: Straight list-price rises came only from smaller vendors, from Airbyte doubling Standard to small steps at Lokalise. Most of these records come from PricingSaaS reports, so they show where it looked, not the whole market.

stats_analysis.t: Half the week’s changes left buyers worse off
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that raise prices or cut what is included
stats_analysis.p: Only 14 changes went in buyers’ favour, and the rest were packaging shifts with mixed effects. Price increases outnumbered price cuts 20 to 4.

stats_analysis.t: Limits tightened about twice as often as they loosened
stats_analysis.figNote: changes tagged Limits tighten vs Limits loosen
stats_analysis.p: Cutting allowances was the single most common move of the week, ahead of price increases. Cuts ranged from Vapi’s concurrent calls to API credits at Appfollow, while TheRundown and Ahrefs raised quotas; several of these records come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: AI touched more than a quarter of changes
stats_analysis.figNote: changes involving AI features, models or usage
stats_analysis.p: AI changes ranged from model rates passed through at Together AI and Telnyx to new credit allowances at CommentSold and outcome pricing at Helply. Of the week’s 10 most relevant changes, 2 were AI costs passed through to customers.

Anthropic made its Max plans monthly-only, while BuildBetter and Moxo went annual-only and TermScout required annual prepay on a monthly seat price. Buyers lose flexibility in one direction or the other.

news_trends.t: Free AI usage is being rationed and moved to payers
news_trends.p: The week’s stories describe free allowances shrinking where AI makes them costly, with free usage reappearing as a perk on paid plans. The earlier-stories window for this edition is empty, so this trend rests on this edition’s stories and changes.

news_trends.t: Model churn changes what developers pay
news_trends.p: Retired and replaced models shift bills without any plan change, from Groq and Google restricting older models to hosts repricing popular ones. Deprecations were September’s most common developer-tool change.
